_source: EXPERTISE ROW, written after seeing the sealed errors: ant.doc.json plus three statements an owner of Ant would make (marked [owner]). Not a clean result.
optional: Optional tasks: a task which typically requires an external library to function; the optional tasks are packaged together with the core tasks, and the external libraries each needs must be added to the classpath (e.g. tasks for .NET, ANTLR, EJB, FTP, JUnit, SCM systems, scripting, SSH and image processing). [owner] Every optional task lives here, including the version-control tasks (Perforce, ClearCase, Visual SourceSafe, CCM) and dependency analysis.
compilers: It is possible to use different compilers for compiling a Java source tree: the compiler is selected globally by a property or per task by the compiler attribute, choosing among classic, modern, jikes, jvc, kjc, gcj, sj and similar compiler implementations.
condition: Conditions are nested elements of the condition and waitfor tasks; core conditions (not, and, or, available, uptodate, equals, isset, contains, socket, http and so on) are evaluated to set a property if a certain condition holds true, a generalization of available and uptodate.
rmic: Runs the rmic compiler for a certain class; it is possible to use different rmic compilers, selected by a property or the compiler attribute (default, sun, kaffe, weblogic, forking, xnew).
cvslib: Support for the CVS tasks, which handle packages/modules retrieved from a CVS repository: generating an XML-formatted report of the change logs recorded in a CVS repository, reporting differences between two tags or dates, storing CVS passwords and reading CVS version information.
email: A task to send SMTP email, using either plain text, UU encoding, or MIME format mail depending on what is available, with attachments given as resources; SMTP auth and SSL/TLS require JavaMail and are only available in MIME format.
repository: Repository (no description in the documentation); the manual only mentions repositories as CVS/SVN source repositories and a probe for a Maven repository being reachable. [owner] It is not version control.
taskdefs: The tasks: a task is a piece of code that can be executed, with attributes and nested elements; this holds the core tasks (archive, compile, deployment, documentation, execution, file, property, SCM and other tasks) and the base tasks designed to be extended, such as the base for tasks that include or exclude files by pattern matching and the base for pack tasks. [owner] These are the concrete built-in tasks themselves (copy, javac, jar, exec and the rest), not the engine that runs them.
listener: Listeners and loggers allow the build process to be monitored: a listener is alerted of build/target/task started and finished and message logged events, and loggers extend listeners with output to the console or log file; built-in ones send an e-mail when the build is finished, colorify the build output, pass events to Log4j, or serve big projects.
types: Concepts and core types used by tasks: description, directory-based filesets, dirsets, filelists, file mappers, filterchains and filterreaders, filtersets, patternsets, path-like structures, permissions, propertysets, I/O redirectors, regexp, resources and resource collections, selectors and tarfilesets.
ant: Apache Ant is a Java-based build tool, kind of like make without make's wrinkles; its core reads a buildfile defining a project with one or more targets, each a set of tasks to be executed, resolves properties, and provides the base task class and the mechanism by which attributes and nested elements of a task are configured. [owner] Only the engine: project, target, the task base classes, property and attribute handling; no concrete task lives here.
ant.util: Ant utilities (no description in the documentation); the manual does not describe the shared utility code used by the core and the tasks.
zip: Support for creating zipfiles (and the jar/war/ear archives based on them) and for unzipping them; note that file permissions will not be stored in the resulting zipfile.
tar: Support for creating tar archives and untarring them, with entries carrying access mode, username and groupname, useful when preparing archives for Unix systems; early versions of tar did not support path lengths greater than 100 characters.
mail: Mail (no description in the documentation as a separate component); the mail task can send plain text mail over SMTP without external libraries.
bzip2: Packs and unpacks a resource using the BZip2 algorithm (the bzip2 and bunzip2 tasks); untar can also unpack BZip2 files on the fly.
